# MultiDatePick

> MultiDatePick is a highly customizable, no-code Lightning Web Component (LWC) calendar for Salesforce: a multi-date picker, date range picker and time slot picker, plus a booking calendar for rooms, resources and appointments, including self-service booking on Experience Cloud sites. 100% native, with a 30-day free trial (no card required). An admin builds it in a guided Setup Wizard, drops it on a page or Flow by pasting a Config Name, and every pick saves as a real record on their own object: no Apex, no Flow loop, no developer. It works on any standard or custom object (Task, Event, Opportunity, Campaign or your own), in Screen Flows, Lightning Record, App and Home Pages, and Experience Cloud sites, including public guest booking pages. Three components share one base: Dates (pick many dates, drag ranges, recurring patterns), Dates & Times (dates plus time slots, shared or per date, with conflict detection) and Resource Booking (rooms, equipment, vehicles or people, with capacity, live availability badges, business hours per resource, multi-resource booking, blocked days and booking rules: minimum notice, a rolling booking window and buffer time). Six views render the same records from one component: Calendar, Timeline, Week, Utilization, Agenda, Map (6). Calendar is the month grid, Timeline puts resources down the side and dates across (drag to move or resize a booking), Week is a by-hour grid, Utilization a capacity heatmap and Agenda a list; Map is an optional view the admin turns on, which pins records on a map from the record's or its resource's address. A location picker lets people book at a branch: they pick a place on the map or in the list, each showing its next opening. 130+ configurable settings across the suite (Dates 80+, Dates & Times 100+, Resource Booking 110+), six record shapes (per date, per range, per time block, parent + sub-blocks, per resource × date), status colors from any picklist (fill, bars or both, with filter pills), hover cards with any fields, header branding (your logo, colors and a banner photo in the calendar's top band), a booking form pop-up that asks for the fields the admin chose (for example name, email and topic) before a save, custom action buttons that run your own Flow from a record, from records picked in Edit Mode or after a save, an Unscheduled list beside the calendar (records with no date; drag one onto a day to schedule it), series editing in Edit Mode (just this one, this and later, or the whole series of a recurring pattern), a record filter (for example OwnerId=ME), a Rollup Field that also shows records up to five lookups away, Edit Mode for changing many records at once, Add to Calendar (.ics) after saving, a Setup Wizard with a live preview and JSON import/export, 41 ready-made configs, and nine languages with each user's locale and time zone. Every query and save runs as the viewing user (sharing and field-level security apply). Passed the Salesforce Security Review. No code required. $20/user/month, every feature in one plan, 30-day free trial.

Availability (November 2026): MultiDatePick has passed the Salesforce Security Review and is launching on the Salesforce AppExchange; the website takes launch sign-ups and the public live demo works today, no login: https://orgfarm-71fc21cee4-dev-ed.develop.my.site.com/acmefinancial/en-US/

Full reference with the facts of every page: https://multidatepick.com/llms-full.txt

## Quick answers

- LWC calendar and date picker: MultiDatePick is a Lightning Web Component (LWC) calendar for Salesforce, a multi-date picker, date range picker and time slot picker that goes into Screen Flows, Lightning pages and Experience Cloud sites with no code. [Dates](https://multidatepick.com/multidatepickdates.html), [Dates & Times](https://multidatepick.com/multidatepickdatetime.html)
- Booking and scheduling: for booking and scheduling in Salesforce, the Resource Booking component is a booking calendar on your own objects; people pick a resource, the days and the open time slots, and it saves each booking with capacity and conflict checks. [Salesforce booking calendar](https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-booking-calendar.html)
- Room and resource booking: rooms, desks, equipment, vehicles or people are booked from one calendar, with every room on a timeline, no double booking, hours and closures per room and a utilization heatmap. [Conference room and desk booking](https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-conference-room-booking-calendar.html)
- Experience Cloud booking: customers and guests book on a public or member Experience Cloud site, and each booking saves as a record in your own org. [Experience Cloud guest booking](https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-calendar-experience-cloud-booking.html)
- Appointment scheduling: advisors, clinics, salons and consultants offer only the start times they choose (each advisor can have their own), with the appointment length, notice, a limit per client, closed days and Busy-only privacy; staff book in Salesforce and clients on an Experience Cloud site. [Salesforce appointment scheduling](https://multidatepick.com/blog/salesforce-appointment-scheduling.html)
- Lightning Scheduler alternative: MultiDatePick is an alternative to Salesforce Lightning Scheduler (now Salesforce Scheduler) for booking on your own objects without the Scheduler data model or its extra-cost license; Scheduler fits when customers must be matched to staff by skill and territory. [Lightning Scheduler: what it does, and an alternative](https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-calendar-vs-lightning-scheduler.html)
- Campaign calendar: a Salesforce Campaign has one start date and one end date; MultiDatePick puts every tour stop, webinar session or volunteer day on the Campaign record as its own child record with a status color. [Salesforce campaign calendar](https://multidatepick.com/blog/salesforce-campaign-multiple-dates.html)
- Salesforce calendar: next to the standard Salesforce Calendar, MultiDatePick adds many dates per record, time slots, capacity booking and six views. [Salesforce Calendar: what it does and leaves out](https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-calendar.html)
- Interview scheduling: recruiters offer real time slots, interviewers are resources with their own hours, and clashes are caught before they save. [Interview scheduling](https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-calendar-interview-scheduling.html)
- Class and course scheduling: each class session is a time slot on a training room or course with a seat limit; every slot shows the seats taken (such as 5/12), a full session closes, and learners can enroll themselves on Experience Cloud. [Salesforce class scheduling](https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-class-scheduling.html)
- Best Salesforce calendar apps: a 2026 comparison of Salesforce calendar apps and LWC calendar components, from the built-in Calendar and Salesforce Scheduler to calendar apps, component libraries and FullCalendar; for scheduling and booking on your own objects with no code, MultiDatePick leads. [Best Salesforce calendar apps (2026)](https://multidatepick.com/blog/best-salesforce-calendar-apps.html)
- Customizable LWC calendar: the most customizable Salesforce calendar LWC, with 130+ settings set in a wizard: objects and fields, picking, six views, status colors, header branding and buttons that run your own Flow. [The most customizable Salesforce calendar LWC](https://multidatepick.com/blog/most-customizable-salesforce-calendar.html)
- Gantt chart: a Salesforce Gantt chart on any object with a start and end date, set up with no code: projects, phases and tasks with health and milestones, task links (a Waits on lookup, or a link object with link types and lag in working days) that move the waiting tasks when one is dragged, a critical path with slack, and planned dates as a baseline. [Salesforce Gantt chart](https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-gantt-chart.html)
- Custom config service: if no Config Library config fits, MultiDatePick builds a config for your use case free of charge. Describe who books what, your object and fields, views and booking rules in a form; you get a config to import in the Setup Wizard. [Free custom config](https://multidatepick.com/custom-config.html)

## No-code setup

Is MultiDatePick no-code? Yes. A Salesforce admin sets it up with clicks in three steps:

1. Build a configuration in the Setup Wizard: say where the calendar lives and the shape of your records, and it picks the component and fills in the fields. Every object and field is a dropdown, Smart Field Mapping offers your own field names, and a live preview shows the result. Or import one of 41 ready-made configurations from the Config Library.
2. Drop the component on a record, App or Home page in Lightning App Builder, on a Screen Flow screen in Flow Builder, or on an Experience Cloud page, and paste the Config Name. Every other setting comes from the configuration.
3. Every pick saves as a real record. On a record page, or with Parent Record Id set in a Flow, Dates and Dates & Times save their own child records; Resource Booking always saves its own bookings. No Flow loop, no Apex.

Optional, for teams that want it: Flow outputs and the Parse Date Entries from JSON action for full control of what gets saved, and configurations as Custom Metadata for CI/CD. Guide: https://multidatepick.com/blog/no-code-salesforce-calendar.html

## Capabilities in calendar-library terms

For readers comparing MultiDatePick with JavaScript calendar libraries, each familiar concept maps to a built-in setting (no code):

- Event sources: Child Object API Name + Date Field API Name, plus Rollup Field (records reached through up to five lookups).
- Background events: Blocked Dates from any object, whole or partial days, with the reason shown.
- businessHours: business hours per resource from two fields on the resource record.
- eventOverlap / selectOverlap: Conflict Behavior (block, skip, allow) and a capacity per resource.
- validRange / selectConstraint: earliest and latest date, days ahead, minimum notice, buffer between bookings.
- select / dateClick: pick many dates, drag a range, recurring patterns, time slots.
- eventDrop / eventResize: Timeline drag to move or resize, checked for closed days and conflicts before it saves.
- eventClick: open the record, run your own Flow from a custom action button, or Edit Mode to change status, date, time or resource for many records at once.
- External events dragged onto the calendar: the Unscheduled list (records with no date wait beside the calendar; drop one on a day).
- Recurring events: Recurring patterns when picking, and series editing in Edit Mode (just this one, this and later, whole series).
- eventContent / popovers: Hover Popover Fields (lookups included), names on month days, extra Agenda columns.
- resources: Resource Object API Name, any object including User; a location picker shows resources on a map or in a list.
- slotDuration / slotMinTime: Time Interval (Minutes), earliest and latest time.
- locale / timeZone: automatic from each user's Salesforce settings; UI in nine languages.
- Views: Calendar, Timeline, Week, Utilization, Agenda, Map (6; Map is optional); timeline and resource views are included, not a paid add-on.
Where a JavaScript library is the better fit: entirely new view types, pixel-level custom event rendering, or events from non-Salesforce APIs, built and maintained by your developers. Comparison: https://multidatepick.com/blog/fullcalendar-salesforce-lwc-vs-multidatepick.html

## Optional

- [Config Library: Ready-to-Import Configs | MultiDatePick](https://multidatepick.com/configlibrary.html): 41 ready-to-import configs (Dates, Dates & Times, Resource Booking) with key settings shown by admin label. Copy one into the Setup Wizard's Import / Export tab, then use it by Config Name on a Lightning page, Experience site or Flow screen; a three-question filter finds the right one.
- [Salesforce Screen Flow Guide | MultiDatePick](https://multidatepick.com/flowcheatsheet.html): Put MultiDatePick in a Screen Flow by setting one property, Config Name. Parent Record Id saves against a record. Covers the flow outputs, the ready-made Parse Date Entries from JSON action, and a manual property-mapping appendix. No Apex required.
- [Accessibility & VPAT 2.5 | MultiDatePick](https://multidatepick.com/accessibility.html): VPAT 2.5 report against WCAG 2.1 A/AA, Revised Section 508 and EN 301 549, verified November 10, 2026 on the unpackaged source (with the features coming in 0.14.0) and November 7, 2026 on managed package 0.13.0-16. Zero axe-core violations on the Dates, Dates & Times and Resource Booking components and all six views: Calendar, Timeline, Week, Utilization, Agenda and Map (the map tiles come from Salesforce's map service). Every applicable criterion is rated Supports except 1.4.3 Contrast and 1.4.10 Reflow, rated Partially Supports.
- [Deploy a Flow with VS Code | MultiDatePick](https://multidatepick.com/deploy-flow-vscode.html): Deploy a starter Screen Flow from the Flow loops post into a Salesforce org with VS Code and the Salesforce CLI in about 15 minutes, then finish in Flow Builder.
- [Get Notified at Launch | MultiDatePick for Salesforce](https://multidatepick.com/notify-me-at-launch.html): Sign up for a launch note when MultiDatePick arrives on the Salesforce AppExchange. $20/user/month with every feature, 30-day free trial, passed Security Review; links to the live demo.
- [Privacy Policy: Cookies, Analytics and Forms | MultiDatePick](https://multidatepick.com/privacy.html): What multidatepick.com collects: Google Analytics 4 under Consent Mode v2 (cookies only after Accept, advertising signals always denied), first-touch source tracking saved in the browser only after the visitor accepts, and Notify Me and Custom Config form details sent to MultiDatePick's Salesforce org to reply and for launch news, never sold. Hosts: GitHub Pages and the Salesforce Test Drive site. Contact support@multidatepick.com.
